data.long_meaning: A Ghazi is a warrior who fights bravely for the cause of Islam, often in a holy war or Jihad. The name Ghazi carries the meaning “Warrior for the cause of God” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Ghazi usually hope their child will grow to embody warrior for the cause of god and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.etymology: Ghazi belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Warrior for the cause of God.”

in_arabic.name: غازی
in_arabic.meaning: المجاهد في سبيل الله، المحارب في الحرب
in_arabic.long_meaning: غازی اسم ہے جو قرآن و حدیث میں ذکر ہوا ہے، اور اس کا مطلب ہے وہ شخص جو اللہ کے راستے میں لڑتا ہے، محارب جو جنگ میں حصہ لیتا ہے، اور شہید ہونے کی امید رکھتا ہے۔ یہ نام اسلامی تقویم میں اہم تاریخی واقعات سے جڑا ہوا ہے، جیسے غزوات النبی صلی اللہ علیہ و آلہ و سلم۔

in_urdu.name: غازی
in_urdu.meaning: اللہ کی راہ میں لڑنے والا، جنگ کرنے والا
in_urdu.long_meaning: غازی ایک ایسا نام ہے جو عربی جڑوں سے نکلا ہے، خاص طور پر غزا (غ ز ا) سے جس کا مطلب ہے لڑنا یا جنگ کرنا۔ اسلامی تاریخ میں، غازی وہ شخص ہے جو جہاد میں حصہ لیتا ہے، اللہ کی راہ میں لڑتا ہے۔ یہ نام جنوبی ایشیائی مسلمانوں کے درمیان مقبول ہے، جہاں یہ مضبوط جنگی جذبے اور روحانی عزم کی علامت ہے۔

in_hindi.name: ग़ाज़ी
in_hindi.meaning: भगवान की लड़ाई लड़ने वाला, योद्धा
in_hindi.long_meaning: ग़ाज़ी नाम की उत्पत्ति अरबी भाषा से हुई है, और यह नाम जिहाद और युद्ध से संबंधित है। इस्लामी परंपरा में, ग़ाज़ी वह व्यक्ति है जो भगवान की राह में लड़ता है, एक योद्धा जो अपने विश्वास की حفاظت के लिए लड़ता है। यह नाम भारतीय मुस्लिम समुदाय में महत्वपूर्ण है, जहां यह बहादुरी और आध्यात्मिक दृढ़ता का प्रतीक है।

in_english.name: Ghazi
in_english.meaning: Warrior, fighter in the way of God
in_english.long_meaning: The name Ghazi originates from the Arabic root 'ghazā' (غ ز ا), meaning to wage war or to strive in the way of God. In Islamic tradition, a Ghazi is a warrior or fighter who engages in jihad, striving in the path of Allah. Historically, Ghazis were soldiers who fought in the Ottoman Empire's military campaigns. The name symbolizes bravery, religious devotion, and a strong sense of justice. It is widely used across Muslim cultures, reflecting a rich heritage of spiritual and martial values.

data.cultural_impact: The title "Ghazi" holds great significance in Islamic history and culture. It represents a warrior who fought courageously to expand the Islamic empire or defend it from external threats. Ghazis were renowned for their bravery, military skills, and strategic brilliance. They would often lead large armies and integrated spiritual devotion into the mission, dedicating their victories to Allah. This cultural impact is celebrated in various forms such as art, literature, and historical narratives.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the title "Ghazi" lies in its connection to the concept of Jihad, or holy struggle, as mentioned in the Quran. A Ghazi is a Muslim soldier who engages in Jihad with the intention of defending Islam, fostering unity among Muslims, and establishing peace and justice in society. By dedicating their lives and actions to Allah, Ghazis believed they were fulfilling one of the most significant commandments in the Islamic faith. This spiritual significance is a reminder of the sacred duty of every Muslim to strive towards righteousness and protect the faith from external harm.
